mandatory_findings.location: Language and appearance cross app and host contracts
mandatory_findings.expected: A directly usable explanation of the typed app-to-native copy path and which localization responsibilities must remain outside feature/native callsites.
mandatory_findings.observed: The body describes keys, plural arguments, complete phrases and native-copy propagation, but does not identify language.t(...), language.plural(...), typed native-translation bundles or nativeT(...). It also does not explicitly explain that locale branches, plural-category selection and grammatical fragment assembly stay out of feature/native callsites. The required contract details therefore remain outside the target flow body.
mandatory_findings.minimal_resolution: Add a concise, attributed paragraph tracing app copy through language.t/language.plural and native copy through shared typed bundles consumed by nativeT. State that locale selection, plural resolution, fallback and interpolation belong in shared modules; feature/native callsites must not branch on locale or concatenate grammatical fragments. Preserve existing English keys/text and the known startup-copy exception. Existing captured evidence suffices: current S10, packages/app-shell/AGENTS.md:23–28, and accepted desktop L2 decisive evidence E10, apps/desktop/AGENTS.md:5–9. No product execution or new investigation is required.

shared_criteria.reason: Prior coverage depths, static conflicts, attributed policy, uncertainty and unexecuted limits are preserved. No source inspection is presented as consumer execution, provider exactly-once behavior or universal security/accessibility proof. Operational invariant controls are not certified.
The artifacts reuse accepted foundations, provide bounded sections and introduce no parallel knowledge framework or fabricated execution/economics evidence.

acceptance_limit: Desktop-web and app-session receive semantic L3 content PASS. Design-tui requires the single stated correction; this review does not support whole-L3 acceptance or L4 release yet.
